Report_ID: Persistence of otitis media with effusion at 4 weeks
Title: a25da0ce_6EF62011BD76414CB99E11BDCC13AE77
Author: Turgut Karlıdağ, İrfan Kaygusuz, Üzeyir Gök, Şinasi Yalçın, Erol Keleş, Levent Öztürk
Comment: The paper reports resolution rather than persistence. Persistence was validly derived as total affected ears minus resolved ears: Group 1, 37-7=30; Group 2, 36-11=25. Outcomes are ear-level and both right and left ears are combined. The paper only reports p>0.05 for the eligible two-treatment-group comparison, so no exact p-value or paper-reported RR was entered.
Topic of Content: Treatment of chronic otitis media with effusion
Participant type: Children aged 2 to 12 years with chronic OME
Outcome measurement: Persistence was derived as failure to meet the paper's resolution definition of restored tympanic membrane mobility plus type A tympanogram (middle-ear pressure at least -100 mmH2O and gradient >0.15)
Outcome variable: Persistence of otitis media with effusion at 4 weeks
additional_group_ns: Group 3 no-treatment observation: 22 patients; 40 affected ears (excluded because it did not receive the same antibiotic co-treatment)
outcome_family: persistence of otitis media with effusion

Title: Montelukast versus inhaled mometasone for treatment of otitis media with effusion in children: A randomized controlled trial
Author: Rahmati et al.
Comment: Persistence counts were derived from explicit Table 2 counts as total minus complete improvement: mometasone 40−33=7 (also 4 relative improvement + 3 no response) and control 44−31=13 (also 11 relative improvement + 2 no response). The reported p=0.416 is an omnibus comparison across all three groups and response categories, so it was not assigned to this direct two-arm dichotomous result. Report_ID: Persistent middle ear effusion defined as post-treatment type-B tympanogram at 4 weeks
Title: Effect of nasal beclomethasone spray in the treatment of otitis media with effusion
Author: Barati et al.
Comment: Ear-level analysis. Combined counts were derived exactly as required by summing the reported right- and left-ear Table 2 cells: case events 13+9=22 of 46+46=92 ears; control events 14+17=31 of 46+46=92 ears. The paper did not report a combined-ear RR, CI, or p-value. The control left-ear cell is printed as 17(34); the count 17 was retained verbatim despite the apparent percentage inconsistency.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Case: amoxicillin plus decongestant plus intranasal beclomethasone spray') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Topic of Content: Treatment of otitis media with effusion
Participant type: Children aged 1-10 years with unilateral or bilateral otitis media with effusion
Recruitment source: Children referred to the otolaryngology outpatient clinic of Al-Zahra Hospital
Outcome measurement: Number of ears with a type-B tympanogram after 4 weeks, summing right and left ears within each arm

Report_ID: Persistent otitis media with effusion, defined as type B tympanogram, combined across both ears at 2 weeks
Title: Efectiveness of mometasone furoate nasal spray on tympanometric results and hearing loss in children with otitis media with efusion
Author: Mohamed Rifaat Ahmed and Wael Elshahat Eldeeb
Comment: The paper reports each ear separately with N=84 children per arm. Following the synthesis contract, right- and left-ear type-B events and denominators were summed: intervention 29+29=58 events among 84+84=168 ear observations; control 59+45=104 among 84+84=168. These ear observations are not statistically independent within children. The Table 2 p=0.006 appears to apply to the multi-category tympanometry comparison rather than specifically to the combined-ear type-B event contrast, so it was not attached to this row.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Mometasone furoate aqueous nasal spray 100 mcg/day plus oral amoxicillin–clavulanate 90 mg/kg/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Pediatric otolaryngology; otitis media with effusion
Study Environment: Otolaryngology Department, Suez Canal University Hospital
Content length: Treatment for 4 weeks; outcome assessed after 2 weeks
Participant type: Children aged 4–12 years with bilateral OME for at least 3 months
Outcome measurement: Type B flat tympanometric curve in either ear, with right- and left-ear counts summed
Outcome variable: Persistent otitis media with effusion, defined as type B tympanogram, combined across both ears at 2 weeks
outcome_family: persistence of otitis media with effusion
